newsitem.title: UKRAINE: FOCUS-Ukraine announces currency trading band.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Ukraine announces currency trading band.

text.p: Ukraine announced a trading band of 1.70 to 1.90 hryvnias against the dollar on Friday, bringing it a step closer to a multi-billion dollar IMF credit, the country's economic policy chief said.

"Today we can say that we will maintain a single rate with the central bank which will be implemented at 1.80, plus or minus 10 points, therefore from 1.70 to 1.90," Deputy Prime Minister Serhiy Tyhypko told reporters.
"It's effective today until the end of the year," he added.

Tyhypko said the move, a first since the former Soviet republic announced independence in 1991, was one of several that Ukraine wanted to implement to boost its chances of getting a $2.5 to $3 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) from the International Monetary Fund.

The international funding body, which completed a week of meetings on Friday, is waiting for Ukraine to pass its 1997 budget and a package of tax reforms to underpin it before it can issue the credit.
Western economists said previously Ukraine had implemented an informal trading band on the hryvnia since its introduction last September.

"This will give a certain stability to Ukrainian producers and to investors who work on the Treasury bill market, and it will also be easier for the government to make budget calculations," Tyhypko said.
The hryvnia was at 1.8410 on the Ukrainian Interbank Currency Exchange on Friday against 1.8430 on Thursday.

"The main thing is for the government to maintain currency stability, but it also needs to look after exporters," said Tyhypko, appointed to his position this month after Viktor Pynzenyk quit in anger over budget delays.

An IMF official said earlier it had made progress during this week's mission to discuss the budget, which was due on January 1, and had moved forward on EFF talks set to continue when President Leonid Kuchma visits Washington in mid-May.
Tyhypko added Ukraine was confident of receiving the credit since it had fulfilled most of the IMF's requirements.
He predicted the budget and several of the new tax laws would be passed by the middle of next month.
